answer.generated: Serializability ensures that a schedule of concurrent transactions appears as if they executed one after another in some order, maintaining the consistency properties of individual transactions. In the given schedule, two-phase locking prevents transactions from holding locks indefinitely and ensures that once a transaction releases a lock, no further updates can occur, thereby preserving consistency from any consistent initial state.
